entries.title: Psalms 112:3
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Righteousness - The fruit or reward of his righteousness, which is God's blessing upon his estate.

entries.title: Psalms 112:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Darkness - In the troubles and calamities of life. He - The upright man.

entries.title: Psalms 112:5
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Lendeth - Gives freely to some, and lends to others according to the variety of their conditions. Affairs - His domestick affairs. Discretion - Not getting his estate unjustly, nor casting it away prodigally, nor yet withholding it from such as need it.

entries.title: Psalms 112:6
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Moved - Though he may for a season be afflicted, yet he shall not be eternally destroyed.

entries.title: Psalms 112:7
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Evil tidings - At the report of approaching calamities.

entries.title: Psalms 112:9
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Dispersed - His goods, freely and liberally. Righteousness - His liberality, or the reward of it. Ever - What he gives is not lost, but indeed is the only part of his estate, which will abide with him to all eternity.

entries.title: Psalms 112:10–113:5
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The desire - Either of the misery of good men; or of his own constant prosperity.
